title: They said “Lord”… and still heard “Leave.”
paragraphs:
You can shout His name…
And still be a stranger to His heart.

You can lift your hands…
And still never surrender your life.

You can look saved on the outside—
…and be completely unknown on the inside.
Here’s the tension you can’t ignore:

What if the most dangerous deception…
is thinking you’re already safe?

What if the scariest words in eternity…
are spoken to people who never doubted their salvation?

“Not everyone who says to Me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of My Father who is in heaven.
Many will say to Me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in Your name, and in Your name drive out demons and perform many miracles?’
Then I will tell them plainly, ‘I never knew you. Away from me, you evildoers!’”

Not rebels.
Not atheists.
Not outsiders.
This is where pride gets exposed.

“I’m good.”
“I go to church.”
“I know Scripture.”
“I serve.”
But Jesus isn’t impressed with your résumé.
Because this is not about weak faith.
Who post Bible verses… but hide private compromise.
Who look holy in public… but negotiate with sin in secret.
They start believing their own performance.

You can operate in spiritual activity
…without being spiritually alive.

You can move in gifts…
…but not walk in obedience.
“Did we not prophesy… drive out demons… perform miracles?”
This is not about performance failure.
“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing.”
“Having a form of godliness but denying its power. Have nothing to do with such people.”
And here’s where it cuts deep.
Sometimes it looks like quiet confidence in your own goodness.

Pride convinces you you’re safe…
when you’ve never truly surrendered.

The Pharisee stood by himself and prayed: “God, I thank you that I am not like other people…”
…But the tax collector stood at a distance… “God, have mercy on me, a sinner.”
Jesus said: “This man, rather than the other, went home justified before God. For all those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
Only one walked away right with God.
But gives grace to the humble.
“God opposes the proud but shows favor to the humble.”
Because if all you hear is warning…
But if you hear Jesus fully…
We are not saved by what we say.
We are saved by Jesus Christ alone.
“For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast.”
“For the grace of God has appeared that offers salvation to all people. It teaches us to say ‘No’ to ungodliness and worldly passions…”
And this is where everything changes.
Jesus didn’t come to build religious performers.
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

Your sin.
Your hypocrisy.
Your secret life.
Your pride.
And He didn’t just expose it.
So you don’t have to stay the same.

Religion says: Perform so you can be accepted.
Jesus says: Come broken, and I will transform you.
“Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here!”
“My sheep listen to my voice; I know them, and they follow me.”
This is not about flawless behavior.
This is about a surrendered heart.
If everything external was stripped away…

No titles.
No ministry.
No image.
No audience.
Would there still be a real relationship between you and Jesus?
Or just an identity you’ve learned to maintain?
“Just as people are destined to die once, and after that to face judgment…”

“Jesus… I don’t want to just say ‘Lord.’
I want You to actually be my Lord.”
But because He paid for it.
Because He’s not looking for perfect people.
When you truly come to Him—
He doesn’t say, “I never knew you.”
“Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
